references.text: The Lord requires that Israel fear Him, walk in His ways, and keep His commandments and statutes for their own good - the same theme of fearing the Lord and obeying His commands.
The Lord expresses His desire that the people always fear Him and keep His commands so that it may go well with them - the same promise of blessing through reverence for God.
A command to keep the Lord's laws and statutes so that it may go well with Israel and they may live long in the land - the same connection between obedience and blessing.
The one who keeps the Lord's statutes and laws shall live by them - the same theme of life through obedience to God's commands.
Israel must keep all the commandments so that they may live and become numerous - the same link between keeping the commandments and life.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom - it expands on the meaning of reverence for God mentioned in Deuteronomy 6:24.
David teaches about fearing the Lord and promises a good life to those who fear Him - the same connection between reverence for God and blessing.
Fear the Lord and turn away from evil; this brings health and strength - the same theme of blessing through reverence for God.
Paul writes about fulfilling the law through love - a New Testament perspective on the fulfillment of the law for good.
The same context - Israel must fear the Lord and keep His statutes all their days so that it may go well with them.
